title: Cambridge Dictionary Names 'Human' Its 2026 Word of the Year
description:
Cambridge Dictionary has named "human" its 2026 Word of the Year, reflecting growing concerns about artificial intelligence and its impact on what it means to be human. "AI is changing how we talk about being human," said Colin McIntosh, the dictionary's lexicographer. "Fears about what humans may lose when we outsource our thinking have made us reconsider the extent to which we rely on AI: from top mathematicians to teachers of young children." The Associated Press reports: The adjective derived from the Latin "humanus" and in use since the 1450s is defined by Cambridge as "having the qualities, faults and feelings that people have, as opposed to gods, animals or machines." [...] Other word contenders for 2026 included "agent," for an AI system that can make decisions and operate without human control and "analogue" for experiences or objects not involving the internet or digital technology.





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: Waymo Robotaxis Pulled From Freeways Indefinitely
description:
Waymo has temporarily suspended freeway operations across all its robotaxi markets after California regulators ordered the company off the state's highways over repeated incidents involving construction zones. The restriction follows a June recall (PDF) of nearly 3,800 vehicles and subsequent software updates (PDF) that failed to prevent further incidents, including a robotaxi driving past a California Highway Patrol rolling roadblock. Ars Technica reports: "Safety is at the foundation of everything we do," Waymo told Ars. "Following recent freeway construction zone encounters on U.S. 101 in California that did not involve any injuries or collisions, the California DMV has implemented an operating restriction on freeway operations in the state. In alignment with our safety-first principles, we have also temporarily restricted freeway operations across our other operating markets to evaluate our performance. Our ride-hailing service continues to operate safely on surface streets, serving over half a million trips each week. We are working with the California DMV and other state officials diligently and responsibly to resume freeway operations."
 
Waymo also told Ars it was continuing to work with the various California agencies that regulate transport. Until the suspension, Waymo was only conducting highway operations in Los Angeles and the Bay Area in California, as well as in Arizona.





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: Jensen Huang's Fall Hits 'Open' Models In Boost to Anthropic and OpenAI
description:
Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia could weaken the open AI model ecosystem he spent years championing, potentially strengthening closed-model developers like OpenAI and Anthropic, according to the Financial Times. From the report: The US chip giant's former chief threw Nvidia's balance sheet into creating a broad AI ecosystem, including by seeding and acquiring start-ups involved in the development of open-source and open-weight models, which users can customize and run on their own hardware. Huang was a forceful advocate for their spread, lobbying against Washington's moves to restrict the use of Chinese-made open models while seeking the development of US alternatives. "Our AI leadership will be judged not by one frontier AI model, but by whether the United States builds a strong, open ecosystem that diffuses into every sector," he wrote this summer in his first-ever message on X.
 
His ignominious exit from Nvidia deprives the open model sector of its most vocal and influential supporter in the US. "I think Jensen stood to gain the most economically and was personally committed to diversity at the model layer," said one venture capitalist who has invested in AI start-ups alongside Nvidia. "Without him and a less generous Nvidia in terms of investment, we may end up in a much more concentrated world of model providers."
 
Whether Nvidia will continue the rapid pace of dealmaking under a new leader is unclear. The company was expected to participate in or lead four start-up deals currently under discussion: investments in Thinking Machines Lab and Groq, a potential partnership with Reflection AI and the $12.9bn acquisition of open model repository Hugging Face. "Jensen drove supply chain brilliantly at Nvidia, but many of those deals were a handshake with Jensen, not a written contract," said Elon Musk in a post on X on Saturday. "Without Jensen, at least some of those critical deals will be lost."
 
"In some sense [Huang leaving Nvidia] is bad for the industry, but in some sense Jensen is an enemy of the frontier labs because he wants models to become commoditized so he retains the prime position in the value chain," said one senior figure at a leading Silicon Valley AI company.
 
"I don't think open weight models are going away... but losing Jensen as their greatest financial backer and champion will slow their progress, and I imagine will not hurt Anthropic's IPO," said another industry figure.
 
"It's reasonable to expect the ouster of Jensen will concentrate computing power more in the hands of frontier labs and hyperscalers," added a senior figure at an AI lab. "That's good for the labs."





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: NGINX2Root: Remote Code Execution vulnerabilities in nginx
description:
Xint is reporting that
it has discovered a collection of five
critical vulnerabilities in the NGINX web
server. The worst flaw, it says, would allow
an unauthenticated attacker to execute commands on an affected nginx server with
HTTP/2 enabled. The company also reports a local-privilege escalation (LPE) kernel
vulnerability, which was introduced in the 4.15 kernel, in the Stream Control Transmission
Protocol (SCTP) subsystem. If chained with the NGINX vulnerability,
it would allow an attacker to gain root privileges on the host. A kernel patch for this
is not yet available.


We also obtained a root shell on the host in a setup where nginx was running in
a Docker container. On many Linux distributions, the SCTP module is installed by
default and the kernel loads it automatically the first time a program opens an
SCTP socket. Whether SCTP is reachable on a given host still depends on the
kernel, the available modules, and the container's restrictions. Where it is
reachable, the attacker can take over the host kernel. Since all containers on
the host share that kernel, this gives the attacker control of the host and
every container on it.


Xint recommends updating to NGINX
1.31.9, which was just released, and to
block the SCTP module on hosts that do not need it until a kernel fix is
available. See the mitigations
section of their report for more information.

title: Satya Nadella Says He's AGI-Pilled Now
description:
An anonymous reader quotes a report from The Verge: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella says he's AGI-pilled, at least when it comes to how AI might make startling changes to the structure of the economy and how politics might change because of it. "I am AGI-pilled in the sense that at an economy level, what is the political economy's organization around AGI?" he asked at a roundtable discussion following his Microsoft Ignite keynote at the Chase Center in San Francisco. But Nadella doesn't think frontier models like Claude are conscious. "I don't think so," he said, adding that he follows Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman's view that companies should not give rights to models and treat them like they might have a moral status, which companies like Anthropic do as a matter of principle. Suleyman has told me he thinks Anthropic's team has "wireheaded" themselves, and that this approach is dangerous. Nadella wasn't quite as firm about it. "It's a good debate," he said. "I'm not sort of dogmatic about it. What I'm saying is the most important social technical issue we have to deal with is how do you ensure that an economy can diffuse this technology broadly?"
 
I asked Nadella how he was thinking about AI after hearing his response to another reporter's questions about Anthropic releasing more products in its office suite. Nadella talked at length about the potential collapse of the economy and the end of democracy if one AI model were allowed to achieve monopoly status. "If the Marxist sort of view is that there's only one firm, then it's over, right? For all of us." "Most people think about this as a competition between tech firms, which of course it will be," he said. "But remember, the model has no limits. It'll be a healthcare company. It can be a financial services company. It can be anything if it wants to be. It can take over the government. Thinking of this as some narrow competition between tech firms, of who is going to get to the next trillion dollars of market cap, is one of the strangest, narrowest ways to think about it."
 
Nadella went on to say that the very nature of companies stood to be disrupted in the future. "If intelligence has network effects, what is the future of a firm?" he asked. "If the model sees anything and learns it, and essentially all of human capital collapses into token capital, what is the role of a firm and the human capital in a firm? That's the debate." "I think the political economy is going to get more and more interesting in that context. No one -- at least in a democracy -- can even win an election if this just goes that way, if there's only capital and there's no labor. I mean, I don't know, that's not an economy." "If the Marxist sort of view is that there's only one firm, then it's over, right? For all of us. Not just for me. You are also going to somehow be some affiliate of Anthropic."





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: Voyager 1 Reaches One Light-Day From Earth
description:
NASA's Voyager 1 has become the first human-made object to travel one light-day from Earth, or 16,094,799,096 miles (25,902,068,356 kilometers). This means radio signals will take 24 hours to reach the spacecraft, now nearly 50 years into its mission. "Since light is essentially the maximum speed in the universe (absent using devices like wormholes, or quantum-physics puzzles), it's a big deal -- so big that NASA will be celebrating the milestone by asking fans to shine Morse Code signals at the sky," reports Space.com. From the report: But why will Voyager 2 take nearly a decade longer? It comes down to choices made for speed and science during the twin missions' nearly 50-year journey, specifically during the first bit when they were flying by planets. The result is Voyager 1 is zooming out at a speed of 3.5 Earth-sun distances (astronomical units a year), while Voyager 2 has a more stately speed of 3.1 Earth-sun distances, according to NASA.
 
[...] At any rate, these fast speeds allowed both spacecraft not only to go fast, but to eventually reach interstellar space in 2012 (Voyager 1) and 2018 (Voyager 2), respectively. With the light-day milestone now reached by Voyager 1, it is anticipated the spacecraft could work into the 2030s, as long as their nuclear power sources can last.
 
NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory, which manages the mission, has been carefully turning off instruments as required, and recently did a "Big Bang" procedure on both spacecraft to redistribute power supplies as best as possible. The idea is to maximize science return on both spacecraft, the only interstellar messengers we have, for as long as possible.





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: Hacker Pleads Guilty to Leak of Grand Theft Auto VI Footage
description:
Artion Kurtaj, the British hacker responsible for leaking early footage of Grand Theft Auto VI in 2022, pleaded guilty Monday to six offenses stemming from cyberattacks against Rockstar Games, Uber and Revolut. The 21-year-old, who was previously deemed unfit to stand trial due to severe autism, carried out the hacking spree "using a mobile phone and an Amazon Fire Stick connected to a hotel room television," reports The Record, "despite bail restrictions limiting his access to the internet." From the report: Now 21, he admitted six offenses at Woolwich Crown Court on Monday, four under the Computer Misuse Act, one of fraud and one of possession of a mobile phone in prison, and is due to be sentenced next week. Kurtaj "used sophisticated hacking techniques to carry out a sustained campaign of cyberattacks, causing serious disruption to major international business and putting sensitive information at risk," said specialist prosecutor Robert Hutchinson.
 
"The defendant was involved in a hacking group responsible for attacks which caused millions of dollars in losses. His offending was calculated and, even after being charged with serious offenses, he continued to target organizations, demonstrating a persistent disregard for the harm he was causing and the law. This was an exceptionally complex and challenging case, but despite his efforts to conceal his identity online, our specialist prosecutors were able to work closely with the City of London Police and international law enforcement partners to build a strong case that exposed his actions and resulted in his guilty pleas," said Hutchinson.





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: US Officially a Measles Endemic Country
description:
An anonymous reader quotes a report from The Hill: The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) confirmed Tuesday that it was withdrawing the U.S.'s measles elimination status, ending more than two decades of what is considered to be one of the greatest public health achievements in modern history. The U.S. met with PAHO's Measles and Rubella Elimination Regional Monitoring and Re-Verification Commission for a three-day, closed-door meeting last week. "The commission concluded that the endemic measles transmission has now been reestablished in Bolivia, Mexico and the United States, and recommended that their measles elimination status be withdrawn, a recommendation which I have accepted," Jarbas Barbosa, PAHO's director, said during the briefing Tuesday. The U.S. achieved measles elimination status in 2000 and has held onto that for more than 25 years. But the past two years have seen close to 8,000 measles infections and roughly a dozen related deaths. This year has been the worst in terms of transmission in more than 30 years.

Erica Schwartz, director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has previously said losing elimination status won't lead to changes in the federal response.
 
"We know where transmission is occurring and we've invested $100 million in state and local health departments to reach those communities," Schwartz said on Tuesday. "Losing a designation doesn't mean we abandon an evidence-based approach. It means we remain focused on stopping outbreaks."





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: Nvidia Rejects Jensen Huang's Offer to Return as CEO
description:
Nvidia's board has unanimously rejected former CEO Jensen Huang's offer to return, despite public support from President Trump and prominent Silicon Valley figures. The decision came as Nvidia reported blockbuster third-quarter revenue of $116 billion, double the year-earlier figure. The Associated Press reports: The embattled company's board of directors "unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO," Nvidia Chairman Harvey Jones said at the start of Nvidia's quarterly earnings call before yielding to Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress, who is running the company as a permanent replacement is sought. [...] Earlier on Tuesday, Huang said in a social media post that if the board decided that his return was in the best interest of shareholders, employees, the company and the country, he would be "honored to answer these calls." He acknowledged making "serious mistakes" in his personal life.
 
The turmoil notwithstanding, Nvidia blew past Wall Street expectations for the third quarter, pulling in $116 billion in revenue, double the level from a year ago. The company also posted net income of $2.70 per share, beating estimates of $2.48 per share. Nvidia stock shot up 5.2% in after-hours trading. Referring to Huang's replacement, Jones said, "We want to install the permanent CEO as quickly as possible, but we won't expedite the CEO before finding exactly the right person." Nvidia also announced a new board committee overseeing national security and trade compliance amid investigations into alleged AI chip smuggling to China.
 
Further reading: Nvidia Stopped Disclosing Singapore Sales As Revenues Hit $104 Billion





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: Google To Keep Temporary Gemini Chats For Two Months
description:
timob58 shares a report from TechCrunch: Google is extending how long it keeps temporary Gemini chats and conversations made with chat history turned off to around two months, saying the change aims to improve safety and security as AI systems become more capable. The change, which will roll out globally in the Gemini app over the coming weeks, marks a significant increase from the previous 72-hour retention period mentioned in Google's Gemini Apps Privacy Hub, according to an archived version from November 12. OpenAI, by comparison, says it may keep temporary chats in ChatGPT for up to 30 days, whereas Anthropic retains incognito chats in Claude for 30 days by default.
 
Google did not answer questions about what prompted the change and whether it would affect how conversations are accessed or reviewed, instead pointing to a blog post that says chats are kept longer to respond to users, process feedback, and protect its services and users. Its updated Gemini Apps Privacy Hub also cites potential system failures as a reason for retaining chats and says temporary conversations are not used to train AI models. "A recent explainer on AI and business IP notes that providers keep data for abuse monitoring even when it is not used for training," adds timob58.





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: Optimizely Hack Turns World's Biggest Websites Into Malware Dispensers
description:
PattonPending writes: As reported by The Register, Zoom, the BBC, CNN, HSBC, and numerous other websites briefly served malware on November 16 after an attacker exploited Optimizely's "Experiments" feature to inject JavaScript into their pages through Optimizely's CDN. The malware replaced cryptocurrency addresses, attempted to steal credit card information and cookies, and sought to compromise iOS devices. Websites belonging to at least 178 organizations were affected via the "OPTIMJACK" vulnerability, which has since been patched. "Earlier today, Optimizely identified a security incident in which an unauthorized party exploited a vulnerability in Experimentation and used it to add malicious JavaScript to some customer projects," the company said. "We've fixed the vulnerability and removed the injected code from affected projects. We've also taken steps to secure affected user accounts and put additional protections in place to prevent unauthorized code from being delivered."
 
The researchers said they found malicious code in 188 of the 1,611 Optimizely scripts examined, including those on the company's own website and login portal, suggesting the number of affected businesses could be significantly higher.





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: Nvidia Stopped Disclosing Singapore Sales As Revenues Hit $104 Billion
description:
Nvidia stopped separately disclosing its Singapore sales (source paywalled; alternative source) after changing its geographic revenue reporting methodology from customer billing addresses to headquarters locations, obscuring a business that generated $104 billion in external revenue in 2025, up 72% from the previous year. The Financial Times reports that the change has drawn scrutiny amid U.S. investigations into whether Singapore-based Megaspeed helped smuggle Nvidia chips into China. From the report: "There is now a lot more focus on Nvidia's Singapore business and questions about who its end customers are," said an investor who is investigating Nvidia's dealings in south-east Asia. The Singapore accounts show that the subsidiary booked $117.8 billion of revenue in the 12 months to January 2026, including $13.6 billion of sales to another Nvidia company. Given the nature of the Singapore operation as a global hub, customers it serves are from all over the world. Only a small quantity of the chips Nvidia sells ends up in or goes through Singapore. The Singapore subsidiary generated just $53 million of profit in the year to January 2026, suggesting limited scope for Nvidia to benefit from Singapore's low corporate tax rates.
 
[...] Singapore's outsized role as a revenue generator for Nvidia used to show up in the company's overall results. In January 2025, the US company reported that Singapore was its second-biggest geographic area by revenue, based on customer billing location. The Singapore office generated $23.7 billion of revenue, behind only the US and representing 18 per cent of global income, based on customers' billing location. The annual accounts said that most of the business was generated by customers using the Singapore office to centralize invoicing and that most of the products were shipped elsewhere, with less than 2 per cent of revenue tied to chips that landed in the city-state.
 
As recently as July last year, Nvidia reported that the Singapore office accounted for 22 per cent of total revenue. This was around the time Nvidia said it began cutting ties with Megaspeed, following US Department of Commerce investigations into the business. Nvidia then changed its financial reporting methodology and stopped splitting out revenue that went to the Singapore office. Before the 2025 reporting change, Nvidia said in its financial filing that it booked sales based on the billing locations of its customers, but that the end customer's location "may be different than our customer's billing location." It added that "most shipments associated with Singapore revenue were to locations other than Singapore and shipments to Singapore were insignificant," according to the filings.





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: Highly Classified NSA Network Goes Down
description:
"CNN and other outlets are reporting that a classified network at the NSA is down," writes longtime Slashdot reader frdmfghtr. "This follows a week of major outages at Microsoft, the FAA, and JPMorgan Chase." From a report: The network, called NSANet, allows employees to communicate classified information internally. At this point there is no evidence of a cyberattack, sources said. As the agency works to understand the scope of the problem, it has enacted staggered arrivals for personnel, the sources said.
 
"We see no evidence that this was a cyberattack," White House spokesperson Lauren Bis said Tuesday on Newsmax. "There is no crisis, or anything like that, for Americans to be worried about." [...] The US shares intelligence with a group of countries in what is known as the Five Eyes intelligence-sharing alliance, which includes the US, UK, New Zealand, Australia and Canada. That intelligence sharing system has not been impacted as a result of the NSANet outage, according to a source from one of the countries and a former US intelligence official. The NSA released a statement addressing the network issues: "The National Security Agency experienced temporary degradation during scheduled routine maintenance. While some internal systems were affected, mission-critical capabilities remain fully operational and our ability to defend national security continues. NSA's infrastructure is designed with multiple layers of redundancy to maintain operations during planned maintenance or unexpected events."





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: School Phone Bans Are Gradually Improving Test Scores
description:
An anonymous reader quotes a report from The New York Times: School cellphone bans are beginning to modestly improve students' academic performance, according to the first large national analysis that compared students' test scores before and after the bans. Schools with strict bans -- requiring students to lock their phones in pouches all school day -- saw math and reading scores improve as if students had an additional week or two of school a year, the study found. It was published Tuesday by the Center for Education Policy Research at Harvard.
 
U.S. students' test scores began falling over a decade ago. The drop coincided with the rise of smartphones, raising questions about their role in the decline. The evidence so far on the academic effects of phone bans has been mixed. But the new study indicates they are starting to have an influence.
 
The study looked at 3.3 million students between 2021 and 2026. They were in third through 10th grade, attending 4,600 U.S. schools. Using scores on MAP tests, which track achievement from fall to spring, it compared the performance of students at schools that put in strict phone bans with those at similar schools that did not have such bans. The annual gains reversed about half the annual loss that an average student experienced in the years leading up to the pandemic. (Students lost even more ground during pandemic closures.) "The earlier studies on cellphone bans have been dismissed as implying small impacts, and in-school cellphone use has been ruled out as playing a big role in the decline," said Thomas Kane, a professor at the Harvard Graduate School of Education and an author of the study. "But we think that's mistaken."





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: Jensen Huang Says He'd Be 'Honored' to Return As Nvidia CEO
description:
In a post on X today, former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says he would be "honored" to return to the company if its board gives the approval. "I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life," he says. "I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board's independent investigation."
 
Huang resigned from the company last week after acknowledging multiple affairs, including one with a women whom U.S. intelligence officials suspect of being a Chinese spy. NPR reports: His comments come as some in Silicon Valley have tried to argue that Huang was pushed out of the company too quickly, and circulated a petition to "stand with Jensen."
 
"We don't want rushes to judgment. We don't want political pressure from the left or the right to force a board into action before we've even taken the time to turn over the cards and learn what was done," said Brad Gerstner, the founder and CEO of Altimeter Capital, an investor in Nvidia, at Semafor's Silicon Valley and the World conference on Monday. The report notes that Huang and Nvidia's general counsel Tim Teter will answer questions behind closed doors before three congressional committees on December 1 and 2.





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: BugMeNot Calls It Quits
description:
BugMeNot, the password-sharing service launched in 2003 to help users bypass website registration requirements, has shut down without explanation after more than two decades. All that's left on the website is a farewell message that reads: "Thanks to everyone who envisioned a better internet." heise online reports: Founded by Guy King, the service had been online since 2003: BugMeNot was a collection of login credentials for various online services. Volunteers submitted credentials they had created for different websites.
 
The idea was simple: Nobody wants to create a full account and provide all their sensitive information just to use a service occasionally. Two decades ago, this privacy concern was more firmly embedded in the public consciousness, but it has since faded considerably. Back then, usernames and passwords were usually the only access controls, so people could easily submit those credentials. Multifactor authentication was still exotic, and passkeys were a distant prospect.
 
The once-popular service lost its shine after just a few years. Service providers quickly discovered and blocked most of the credentials. They could also prevent users from saving logins for their services directly through BugMeNot, for example when those services were paid. More modern security mechanisms also emerged in recent years. As a result, credentials found on BugMeNot rarely worked. Most online providers also blocked the service's disposable email addresses under @bugmenot.com, making them rarely usable. Many people forgot about the site. Now its operators have shut it down without giving a reason. Additional discussions about BugMeNot's closure can be found on Reddit and Hacker News.





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: Redict deprecated in favor of Valkey
description:
Drew DeVault has
announced that
Redict, a fork of Redis that was created in response to
Redis's 2024 license change, has been deprecated. He recommends switching to Valkey, the permissively licensed Redis fork supported by the Linux Foundation. The two projects are mutually compatible, so switching should be as simple as changing which package is installed and renaming the configuration file.




I had hoped to rally the Redis diaspora around a copyleft initiative, to protect ourselves from future rug-pulls, and made Redict to serve this purpose. However, with the valkey project's success, and Redis's return to a copyleft license, Redict was not able to build a sustainable community.


We recommend that Redict users switch to valkey, which uses a permissive license but has better long-term prospects. We advise against switching back to Redis; though it is once again open source, and copyleft, it uses a contributor license agreement which will facilitate another rug-pull when Redis has a bad financial quarter.

title: [$] Zellij manages terminal workspaces with style
description:
Zellij is a relatively new entrant in the
terminal-multiplexer
category. Like GNU
Screen and tmux it gives
users the ability to manage a workspace inside a terminal with split panes,
provides session management, and so forth; but Zellij also includes a web server for
browser access to a terminal session, is extensible via a plugin API, and is likely
more beginner-friendly than its predecessors. Its most recent release, version 0.46,
adds a standalone terminal emulator, a built-in inbox for notifications, and a settings
screen so users can configure the application without fussing with
configuration files. While the low version number might suggest that it is not
yet ready for serious use, it seems stable and full-featured enough to
meet the needs of many users.

description: Why efforts of setting up Agama-Proxy.service on top of F45 Server (bare metal ) are worth full ?
